fixes.explanation: The text says, “The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, and sat down on his throne.” (1 Kings 2:19) The KING gets up when his mother walks in. He stands, he bows, and THEN he sits. Solomon has a whole kingdom, and he still moves faster than I do when my oven timer goes off.

Right on. “…the king had a throne brought for his mother, who sat down at his right hand.” (1 Kings 2:19) Solomon doesn't just find her a spot. He has a whole THRONE brought in. In the junk drawer I used to live in, the best seat I ever got was a pile of takeout menus with an expired coupon leaning on my shoulder. Nobody brought ME a throne. Not even a stool with a good attitude.

problems.problem: The reaction is still mild and lacks a strong punchline.
The drawer-and-throne contrast is still mild, without a stronger laugh.
